claims.text: The most dangerous form of suicidal desire is caused by the simultaneous presence of thwarted belongingness and perceived burdensomeness, along with hopelessness about these states.
The capability to engage in suicidal behavior is separate from the desire to engage in suicidal behavior.
The capability for suicidal behavior emerges via habituation and opponent processes in response to repeated exposure to physically painful or fear-inducing experiences.

evidence.description: We propose that the most dangerous form of suicidal desire is caused by the simultaneous presence of two interpersonal constructs-thwarted belongingness and perceived burdensomeness (and hopelessness about these states)
...and further that the capability to engage in suicidal behavior is separate from the desire to engage in suicidal behavior.
According to the theory, the capability for suicidal behavior emerges, via habituation and opponent processes, in response to repeated exposure to physically painful and/or fear-inducing experiences.

methodologies.name: Interpersonal Theory of Suicidal Behavior
methodologies.description: A theoretical framework proposing explicit, falsifiable hypotheses distinguishing the desire for suicide from the capability for suicide.

limitations.text: Suicidal behavior has received relatively little empirical attention due in part to a relative absence of theoretical development.

future_work.text: Scientific inquiry and potential empirical falsification of the delineated hypotheses of the interpersonal theory of suicide.
